proposal.utterance: What BFO category best fits 'the normative force of an obligation'?

entities.label: NormativeForce
entities.rationale: Normative force is the capacity or power of an obligation to bind, direct, or compel action. It is internally grounded in the obligation (or its bearer) — it does not merely arise from external social assignment but from the intrinsic character of the norm — and is only manifested when the obligation is acted upon or violated. This fits BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016): a realizable entity that is internally grounded in its bearer and that can be realized in a process (e.g., compliance, enforcement). It is distinct from a Role (externally grounded) and from a Quality (not a static measurable property but a directed capacity). The existing class LegalObligation (BFO_0000023, Role) represents the obligation itself; NormativeForce would be a distinct specifically dependent continuant inhering in the obligation or its bearer, representing its binding power.

relations.rationale: NormativeForce is a subclass of Disposition: it is a realizable, internally grounded capacity inhering in the bearer of an obligation, realized in processes of compliance, enforcement, or violation.
As a Disposition, NormativeForce is also a Specifically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000020), inheriting the requirement that it inheres in exactly one bearer at any time.

open_questions: Should NormativeForce inhere in the obligation-as-role (i.e., an instance of LegalObligation), or in the material bearer (the person) who holds the obligation? BFO requires SDCs to inhere in a specific bearer.

Is the intended sense of 'normative force' the binding capacity of a norm itself (disposition), or the felt compulsion experienced by an agent (which might be better typed as a PsychologicalLegalManifestation, already in the ontology as BFO_0000020)?
Should NormativeForce be realized in a specific process class such as ComplianceProcess or EnforcementProcess? If so, should those process classes also be minted?

Is this question exploratory (seeking a recommendation) or are you asserting that 'normative force of an obligation' should be added as a class to the working ontology? The answer above assumes you want a concrete proposal.
proposal.rationale_summary: The normative force of an obligation is best categorized as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) rather than a Quality, Role, or Process. A disposition in BFO is a realizable specifically dependent continuant that is internally grounded in its bearer and that is only manifested through a process of realization (e.g., an act of compliance, a legal enforcement proceeding, or a conscientious refusal). Normative force fits this profile: it is not merely an externally assigned function (which would favor Role), nor a static measurable magnitude (which would favor Quality), nor an occurrent event (Process). The closest existing class in the working ontology is LegalLegitimacyCondition or NormOntologicalCondition (both BFO_0000016), but normative force is distinct enough — referring specifically to the binding or action-directing power intrinsic to an obligation — to warrant a new class NormativeForce as a subclass of BFO_0000016 (Disposition). The proposal is conservative: only one new class is minted, and open questions flag the key modeling choices the user must resolve before commitment.
